title: Compare the mixture-swap scaling ladder for Monday's data swap
body:
## TL;DR

The completed d1536 mixture-swap run gives **1.20× macro compute-equivalent speedup** over the old ladder in #8435: **0.91844 BPB, 0.72% lower**, with improvements on **15 of 16 subsets**. Final macro loss is **2.54317**. The d512 mixture-search swarm gives **1.17× macro speedup**, estimated from measured final BPB across three seeds per mix.

| Paloma evaluation | d1536 measured final | d512 swarm estimate |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Macro** | **1.20×** | **1.17×** |
| Code: 100 programming languages | **1.07×** | **1.70×** |
| Academic documents: M2D2 S2ORC | 1.13× | 1.13× |
| Falcon RefinedWeb | 1.15× | 1.10× |
| Dolma v1.5 | 1.14× | 1.16× |

All speedups use BPB and assume equal throughput. Swarm estimates transfer the old ladder’s scaling slopes to d512; they are not measured runtime savings. The swarm helped select this mix and switches after 10% of training, versus 25% in this ladder.

The swarm also measures **1.43% lower mean Uncheatable BPB**, including **5.11% lower on C++** and **2.09% lower on Python**. The old scaling ladder has no Uncheatable baseline, so we cannot fit an Uncheatable speedup curve. Swarm methods and source data are below.

Completed d768/d1024 runs improve macro BPB by 0.41%/0.70%, but code BPB regresses at both widths. At d1536, code BPB improves by 0.46%; the largest code gain remains in the d512 swarm. Wikipedia is the only d1536 regression, at 0.50% higher BPB. Recipe differences and pre-swap comparisons are in the details.

[![Paloma scaling comparison with measured finals](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/final-2026.09.15.1/paloma-scaling-bpb.png)](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/final-2026.09.15.1/index.html)

[Interactive plot](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/final-2026.09.15.1/index.html). All points are measured finals: gold is the new-mixture ladder, blue is the original ladder, each at d768/d1024/d1536. Labels show compute-equivalent speedup: **1.20×** means the original-mixture baseline needs 20% more compute to match that point’s quality. d512 is omitted to keep the y-axis focused on the larger models.

[d1536](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/h100-mix25-20260912-d1536) finished all 90,767 updates and its final evaluation on September 15. The final evaluation is logged at zero-indexed step 90,766.

## Mixture phases

- **0–25%:** Harrier, emphasizing software, science, history, and math.
- **25–80%:** More command-line agent transcripts, law, and news; less general web code, finance, history, and math.
- **80–100%:** More natural-science research and data in the highest classifier-rated quality bucket, while retaining the emphasis on low-level code and agent transcripts.

Percentages refer to training steps; transitions round to mixture-block boundaries.

<details>
<summary>Phase weights, topic labels, and quality shares</summary>

Each phase weights 200 topic × quality groups. Topic shares below sum over quality buckets; quality shares sum over topics. Topic names describe the dominant content in each cluster, using the [store’s labels and examples](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/harrier-k40-cluster-overview/2026.08.18/index.html?revision=uniform-sampling).

- **Start to 25% — Harrier:** Software-heavy, led by infrastructure/security (9.3%), performance logs and low-level code (9.0%), and natural-science research (8.8%). General software development/web code contributes 7.9%; history/literature 6.9%; math problems/proofs 4.3%.
- **25% to roughly 80% — new phase 0:** More command-line agent transcripts (1.3% → 6.0%), law/courts (1.1% → 3.6%), and world news (0.8% → 2.7%). Less general software development/web code (7.9% → 4.5%), finance (5.6% → 2.4%), history/literature (6.9% → 3.7%), and math (4.3% → 1.8%). Performance logs and low-level code become the largest cluster at 10.6%.
- **Roughly 80% to finish — new phase 1:** More natural-science research (6.9% → 11.3%), alongside performance logs/low-level code (11.4%) and agent transcripts (6.6%). General software development/web code falls again, to 3.1%, and math to 1.4%. The highest classifier-rated quality bucket, Q4, rises from 22.9% to 28.0% of the mixture; it was 22.6% in the initial phase.

Arrows compare each phase with the preceding phase. These are configured weights, not measured token counts or claims that every document matches its cluster’s label. [All 40 topic shares and five quality shares](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/mixture-phases-2026.09.13.1/index.html).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Final result versus the prior forecast</summary>

| Estimate | Final macro loss | Final macro BPB | Macro speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Measured d1536 final | 2.54317 | 0.91844 | 1.20× |
| Prior adjusted forecast | 2.54351 | 0.91867 | 1.19× |
| Prior raw forecast | 2.54131 | 0.91798 | 1.21× |
| Original-mixture d1536 final | 2.56377 | 0.92507 | 1.00× |

The adjusted forecast overpredicted final loss by 0.00034 and BPB by 0.00023. It used a linear fit to the 75–95% evaluations, plus the mean final-minus-predicted residual from d768/d1024 using the same window. [Frozen forecast, backtests, and method](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/forecast-2026.09.15.1/index.html) · [Measured final results for all 16 subsets](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/final-2026.09.15.1/final_results.csv).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Swarm comparison: measured endpoints, speedup assumptions, and Uncheatable</summary>

The [pinned swarm snapshot](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/grug-moe-mix-swarm/tree/75c25718e2a7cf7a3b1b498b00479351f80345e0/registry/v1/swarms/h100-d512-from10pct-store-4d2e363d) contains three seeds of the selected `996f489106c7b922` mixture and three seeds of the old Harrier mixture. The selected weights match the ladder’s `best_mixture_996f489106c7b922.json` exactly; old weights match `harrier_mix_2026_08_18.json` within 1.1e-8 per cell. All six runs restore the same step-393 checkpoint after 10% baseline training, then train at the same d512 budget. Metrics below are means of final dropless BPB, not surrogate predictions.

| Evaluation | Old mix BPB | Selected mix BPB | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Macro Paloma | 1.193383 | 1.186012 | −0.62% |
| Code: 100 programming languages | 0.704489 | 0.678921 | −3.63% |
| Academic documents: M2D2 S2ORC | 0.953385 | 0.947892 | −0.58% |
| Falcon RefinedWeb | 1.110216 | 1.105921 | −0.39% |
| Dolma v1.5 | 1.002632 | 0.995775 | −0.68% |
| Macro Uncheatable | 0.877434 | 0.864898 | −1.43% |
| Uncheatable C++ | 0.603348 | 0.572521 | −5.11% |
| Uncheatable Python | 0.548619 | 0.537162 | −2.09% |
| Uncheatable arXiv computer science | 0.877615 | 0.861141 | −1.88% |
| Uncheatable arXiv physics | 0.950631 | 0.922505 | −2.96% |

Paloma compute-equivalent speedup is `(old mean BPB / selected mean BPB)^(1/α)` at equal compute and throughput. It uses the original d768/d1024/d1536 ladder’s per-subset slopes, with zero loss floor; macro α is 0.040007. Applying those slopes at d512 is an assumption, and this swarm helped select the mixture, so it is not independent validation. No Uncheatable multiplier is inferred from Paloma slopes.

[All measured comparisons and calculation inputs](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/swarm-2026.09.14.1/comparison.csv) · [Six source observations](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/swarm-2026.09.14.1/selected_runs.json) · [Reproduction script](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/swarm-2026.09.14.1/analyze.py) · [Input files](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/swarm-2026.09.14.1/index.html).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Measured results, pre-swap comparison, and speedup calculation</summary>

Final snapshot: September 15. All four rungs, d512 through d1536, have finished.

| Final macro BPB | Baseline | New mixture | Change | Subsets improved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| d768 | 1.083720 | 1.079330 | −0.41% | 11/16 |
| d1024 | 1.002217 | 0.995244 | −0.70% | 12/16 |
| d1536 | 0.925068 | 0.918442 | −0.72% | 15/16 |

Macro BPB is the mean across all 16 subsets. At d768, the largest improvements are Twitter AAE (−1.47%), 4chan (−1.22%), and Gab (−0.92%). RedPajama (+1.28%), Penn Treebank (+0.77%), Wikipedia (+0.46%), WikiText (+0.29%), and programming languages (+0.28%) regress. Lower BPB is better.

At d1024, the largest improvements are Twitter AAE (−2.04%), Gab (−1.54%), and 4chan (−1.18%). RedPajama (+0.82%), Wikipedia (+0.37%), WikiText (+0.30%), and programming languages (+0.06%) regress.

The d768 treatment was already 0.61% lower in macro BPB at 20% training, before the switch. Both d768 runs use the same batch and total token budget, so this compares matched token counts. Validation data match across all 16 subsets. Hardware, expert-parallel size, evaluation batch, and some optimizer settings differ; the frozen configurations record the details.

The ladder d512 coordinator repeated its final evaluation after a retry. The comparison uses one final point per run; see the [incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/416).

The speedup calculation recenters and inverts each subset’s plotted baseline fit, following the [MoE guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/agent.md#effective-speedup-calculation). It uses the subset fit’s exponent and zero loss floor, replacing the guide’s macro-loss constants. [Calculation inputs and results](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/h100-mix25-paloma/final-2026.09.15.1/point_speedups.csv).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Run configurations, source metadata, and earlier analyses</summary>

The initial mixture is Harrier 2026.08.18. The data store and simulated epoching stay the same.

All treatment runs use sequence length 4,096, global batch 1,024, and 791 training tokens per active parameter. The d-number is model hidden width. Phase 0 and phase 1 below are the new mixture's two weight sets.

| Rung / W&B run | H100 GPUs | Total steps | New phase 0 starts | New phase 1 starts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [d512](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/h100-mix25-20260912-d512) | 8 | 3,930 | 1,008 | 3,120 |
| [d768](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/h100-mix25-20260912-d768) | 16 | 11,420 | 2,880 | 9,120 |
| [d1024](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/h100-mix25-20260912-d1024) | 32 | 30,552 | 7,680 | 24,432 |
| [d1536](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/h100-mix25-20260912-d1536) | 64 | 90,767 | 22,704 | 72,576 |

The launcher is `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_h100_scaling_ladder.py`; weights are in `best_mixture_996f489106c7b922.json` beside it, extracted from `best-mixture-996f489106c7b922.parquet`. The exact launch source and weights have not yet been published. Mixture metadata: swarm `h100-d512-from10pct-store-4d2e363d`, HF revision `75c25718e2a7cf7a3b1b498b00479351f80345e0`.

- [Original hero scaling report](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/535B-A23B-18T-Token-Hero-Run-Scaling-Ladder--VmlldzoxNzc2MDM5Ng), tracked in #8435.
- [Frozen run configurations and evaluation history](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/issue-9126-paloma-20260912-1220).
- [Earlier 50%-progress analysis](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/Paloma-scaling-comparison:-mixture-switch-after-25%-of-training--VmlldzoxNzkyMTA0MQ==), retained for the pre-swap comparisons.

</details>

## Next steps

- [x] Compare the 95%-based d1536 forecast with its measured final endpoint.
- [ ] Publish the exact launch source and mixture weights.
- [x] Deploy the selected mixture to the hero run from permanent step 108,000 under a new W&B ID; [launch and initial health record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8506#issuecomment-5684891157). The linked record covers launch and initial health.
